rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲟⲩ 'fellow, each-other.' Used here as count noun for members of a four-fold series (1st/2nd/3rd/4th ⲟⲉⲣⲏⲟ) where the four of light are paired with four of darkness. 'Counterpart' captures the pair-correspondence.

Apparently distinct from ⲯⲩⲭⲏ in this passage. ⲯⲛⲉ = the inner identifying essence of each cosmic entity, identified in formula 'his ⲯⲛⲉ is X' with various principles (spirit/light/life for light beings; fire/desire/etc. for dark beings). Possibly a Lycopolitan native term used in contrast to the Greek loan ⲯⲩⲭⲏ which here designates the captive Living Soul.
Verbal noun ⲧ-ⲟⲓⲛ-ⲃⲱⲗ formed on ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release, dissolve' (accumulated vocab). The ⲧⲟⲓⲛ- prefix forms an action-noun. Eschatological term for the cosmic dissolution at the end of times.

Greek loanword ζωγραφία 'painting.' Here = 'depiction of the soul,' the cosmic Image/Statue of the Living Soul gathered at the end — Manichaean technical figure related to the Eikon and the Last Statue.

Likely Greek κλώνη 'branch, twig' or related to Coptic ⲕⲗⲟⲙ 'crown, wreath.' The 'wreath of light' grasps within itself the five elements — a Manichaean image for the bound crown of light-substance distributed through the elemental cosmos.
Standard Coptic idiom 'stand firm/fast on one's feet,' with Lycopolitan ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ for ⲉⲣⲁⲧϥ̄.
Greek στοιχεῖον; technical Manichaean cosmological term for the five light-elements (light, wind, water, fire, ether) bound in matter.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'to burn.' Eschatological term for the great fire that will consume all the constructions of the cosmos.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲛⲁϩⲙ̄ 'to save, rescue.' Paired here with ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('release') in the soteriological vocabulary of unbinding from material chains.
Lycopolitan ⲥⲛⲁⲍ = ⲥⲛⲁⲩϩ 'chains, fetters' (from ⲥⲱⲛⲁϩ 'bind'). Paired with ⲙⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'bonds' as the material-cosmic restraints from which souls are loosed.
Reduplicated form of ⲗⲱⲗⲙ̄ⲥ 'pollute, defile.' Used of the dark king's defilement of the captive light-soul with all his powers.

Greek νόμος + 'of Sin' (Sin capitalized as cosmic principle, per terminology guide). Identifies the fourth dark counterpart as 'the spirit of darkness, the law of Sin' — the cosmic principle of transgression.
